title: Character & Conduct
description: Little Muslim → Beginner. Short questions about respectful words, fairness, trust, privacy, gratitude, cooperation and making amends, using familiar home and classroom situations. Children can ask a trusted adult for guidance and help. Written with children around ages 6–9 in mind; an adult may read questions aloud. All questions are Beginner level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Uses introductory knowledge of good character and conduct, short wording and straightforward examples for the Kids audience. Age and level are editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith reports checked during preparation. Present-day scenarios illustrate ordinary social conduct. Seeking help about harm is distinguished from gossip, and forgiveness is not presented as requiring continued exposure to harm. No question asks children to judge another person’s faith or worth. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Everyday scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: What does the Quran teach about hurtful nicknames?

options.text: Do not use names that insult people
Use them if your friends laugh
Use them for every new classmate
Make the smallest child a target

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches us not to mock people or use insulting nicknames. Names should show respect.

questions.question: Which kind of talk should we avoid?

options.text: Kind words of encouragement
Hurtful talk about someone behind their back
Asking a teacher to explain a lesson
Telling a parent that we need help

questions.explanation: The Quran warns against backbiting. We should protect people's dignity in the way we speak about them.

questions.question: What should we do with something entrusted to us?

options.text: Pretend it has become ours
Hide it so nobody can use it
Return it to its rightful owner
Give it away without permission

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches us to return trusts to their owners. Looking after another person's belongings is a responsibility.

questions.question: Should we be fair only to people we like?

options.text: Yes, only our friends deserve fairness
Yes, fairness depends on who is strongest
No, fairness never matters at all
No, fairness matters even when we dislike someone

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches fairness even when we dislike someone. Feelings do not make unfair treatment right.

questions.question: What kind of work does the Quran tell us to help one another with?

options.text: Good and right actions
Hurting someone together
Planning how to cheat
Hiding another person's belongings for fun

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches cooperation in goodness, not in wrongdoing. Helping should support something good.

questions.question: Before entering another family's home, what should we do?

options.text: Walk straight in without asking
Ask permission and greet them
Push the door open and hide
Insist that every door belongs to us

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches permission and greetings before entering another home. We wait until we are welcome to enter.

questions.question: Which behavior shows humility?

options.text: Looking down on everyone else
Boasting that nobody else matters
Respecting people without acting superior
Refusing kindness to show our importance

questions.explanation: Humility means avoiding arrogance and treating others with respect. The Quran warns against boastful pride.

questions.question: In an ordinary conversation, what kind of voice shows good manners?

options.text: Shouting over everyone for attention
Screaming to stop others from speaking
Being loud only to annoy people
A calm voice suited to the place

questions.explanation: Luqman's advice in the Quran teaches moderation and lowering the voice. We speak considerately in everyday conversation.

questions.question: What does the Quran teach about food and drink?

options.text: Enjoy them without waste
Waste them to show we have plenty
Throw them away for fun
Take far more than we need every time

questions.explanation: The Quran permits eating and drinking while teaching us not to waste. We can handle food thoughtfully.

questions.question: When someone greets us kindly, what does the Quran teach?

options.text: Answer with an insult
Return the greeting equally or better
Always pretend we did not hear
Demand a gift before replying

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches us to return greetings equally or more warmly. A respectful reply is good conduct.

questions.question: What should we do when someone helps us kindly?

options.text: Pretend their effort means nothing
Demand even more before speaking
Thank them
Mock them for helping

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught the importance of thanking people. Gratitude recognizes the kindness we receive.

questions.question: What does the Quran encourage between believers who disagree?

options.text: Keeping every argument going
Inventing insults for both sides
Helping a disagreement become a fight
Making peace

questions.explanation: The Quran encourages making peace between believers. We can seek a fair, calm way to settle disagreements.

questions.question: Which quality does the Quran encourage when someone has wronged us?

options.text: Forgiveness
Endless revenge
Humiliating them forever
Making their family suffer too

questions.explanation: The Quran encourages forgiveness and pardon. Forgiving an ordinary mistake can help us move away from revenge.

questions.question: What did the Prophet ﷺ warn against in the report about hidden wet food?

options.text: Being honest about what is offered
Cheating people
Letting people see what they are buying
Explaining something truthfully

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ warned against cheating. Hiding an important fact to deceive someone is wrong.

questions.question: The Quran says people were made into different peoples and tribes so they could do what?

options.text: Mock every unfamiliar name
Decide that language makes someone worthless
Get to know one another
Refuse to respect anyone different

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches people to know one another. Different backgrounds are not a reason for contempt.

questions.question: How should we speak to someone asking for help?

options.text: With insults because they need something
With laughter at their difficulty
With cruel names to embarrass them
With respect, without harshly driving them away

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches us not to harshly turn away someone asking. We can speak respectfully and involve an adult when needed.

questions.question: When asked to make room in a gathering, what does the Quran teach?

options.text: Make space for others
Spread our belongings across every empty seat
Push people away for fun
Pretend nobody else belongs there

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches making room in gatherings. Being considerate helps others take part too.

questions.question: After giving charity, which behavior should we avoid?

options.text: Letting them keep their dignity
Humiliating the person with hurtful reminders
Giving without showing off
Speaking respectfully to them

questions.explanation: The Quran warns against spoiling charity with hurtful reminders. Giving should not be used to shame someone.

questions.question: When we wrong someone, what should we try to do?

options.text: Pretend their hurt does not matter
Blame them for our own choice
Seek their forgiveness and put things right
Repeat the same wrong for fun

questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ taught us to seek forgiveness for wronging others. We should stop the wrong and work to repair it.

questions.question: How should we treat peaceful people of another faith?

options.text: With cruelty because they are different
With unfair rules just for them
With insults instead of respect
With kindness and fairness

questions.explanation: The Quran permits kind and fair dealings with those who are not fighting us. Different faiths do not justify cruelty.

questions.question: If a nickname hurts a classmate, does making others laugh make it kind?

options.text: No, laughter does not make an insult kind
Yes, laughter makes every name acceptable
Yes, as long as the classmate is quiet
Yes, if a popular child chooses it

questions.explanation: A joke that insults someone can still hurt. Respect matters more than getting laughs at another person's expense.

questions.question: Does avoiding gossip mean hiding bullying from a trusted adult?

options.text: Yes, hurtful behavior must always stay secret
No, getting help for harm is different
Yes, no child may report a problem
No, it means we should invent stories instead

questions.explanation: Reporting harm to get help is different from gossip. Tell a trusted adult when someone is hurting you or another child.

questions.question: Does borrowing something make it ours to keep?

options.text: Yes, borrowing always means owning
Yes, if we like it more than the owner
No, the owner still has a right to it
Yes, if the owner forgets for one day

questions.explanation: Something borrowed still belongs to its owner. We care for it and return it as agreed.

questions.question: Which choice shows fairness during a game?

options.text: Change the rules whenever our team loses
Give only our friends extra turns
Pretend the other team's points do not count
Apply the agreed rules to both teams

questions.explanation: Fairness means applying the agreed rules honestly. Liking one team more does not justify cheating the other.

questions.question: Does being helpful mean joining every plan a friend suggests?

options.text: No, we should help with good, not wrongdoing
Yes, even a plan to hurt someone
Yes, a friend's idea can never be wrong
No, it means refusing every kind action

questions.explanation: Cooperation is for good actions. We can refuse an unkind plan and suggest something better.

questions.question: If a home's door is open, is that always permission to enter?

options.text: Yes, an open door belongs to everyone
No, we still need permission
Yes, we may hide inside without asking
Yes, greetings are never needed at open doors

questions.explanation: An open door does not automatically give permission. The Quran teaches respect for other people's homes.

questions.question: Can we feel pleased about learning well without looking down on others?

options.text: No, doing well means others have no value
Yes, but only if we insult slower learners
Yes, confidence can go with respect
No, we must pretend we can never learn

questions.explanation: Humility does not mean denying our progress. We can be pleased while respecting others and avoiding arrogance.

questions.question: Why should we avoid shouting over people in an ordinary conversation?

options.text: So nobody else ever gets a turn
So we can frighten quiet classmates
So we can stop every useful discussion
So others can speak and listen comfortably

questions.explanation: A considerate voice helps conversation. The Quran's advice encourages moderation instead of needless loudness.

questions.question: Does avoiding food waste mean we must force ourselves to eat too much?

options.text: No, take a suitable amount and handle leftovers wisely
Yes, discomfort never matters
Yes, we must always take the largest portion
No, it means wasting food is always better

questions.explanation: We can avoid waste by taking suitable portions and asking an adult how to save safe leftovers. Eating too much is not the goal.

questions.question: Which response follows the lesson about returning a greeting?

options.text: Turn every greeting into an argument
Answer respectfully instead of mocking the greeting
Ignore others to show we are important
Laugh at the speaker's voice

questions.explanation: Returning a greeting shows respect. The Quran teaches a reply at least as good as the greeting received.

questions.question: Does thanking Allah mean we should never thank a person who helped us?

options.text: Yes, their kindness must be ignored
Yes, gratitude is only for expensive gifts
No, we should thank people too
No, we should demand another gift first

questions.explanation: Thanking people fits the Prophet's ﷺ teaching. Gratitude to Allah does not require ignoring other people's kindness.

questions.question: Which action helps make peace in a small disagreement?

options.text: Carry insults from one side to the other
Make up new reasons to argue
Cheer whenever someone gets hurt
Listen fairly and seek a calm solution

questions.explanation: Making peace means helping people settle a disagreement fairly. It does not mean feeding the argument.

questions.question: Does forgiveness mean we must let someone keep hurting us?

options.text: No, we can get help and stop harm
Yes, harm must continue forever
Yes, asking an adult for help is always wrong
No, it means hurting innocent people instead

questions.explanation: Forgiveness does not require allowing ongoing harm. Ask a trusted adult for help when you need protection or support.

questions.question: If cheating helps us win, does winning make it honest?

options.text: Yes, winners never need to follow rules
No, winning does not make cheating honest
Yes, as long as nobody notices
Yes, a prize makes every trick acceptable

questions.explanation: A result gained by cheating is still dishonest. The Prophet's ﷺ warning teaches us to avoid deception.

questions.question: Does speaking a different language make a child less worthy of respect?

options.text: Yes, only our language deserves respect
Yes, unfamiliar names have no value
No, language is not a reason to look down on someone
No, but mocking their accent is always kind

questions.explanation: Different peoples can learn about one another. A child's language or background is not a reason for contempt.

questions.question: If we cannot provide what someone asks for, can we still respond respectfully?

options.text: No, an insult is always required
No, we must make fun of their need
Yes, but only after embarrassing them
Yes, we can be polite and seek suitable help

questions.explanation: Respectful speech does not require promising everything requested. We can speak kindly and ask an adult about suitable help.

questions.question: Why is making room in a gathering considerate?

options.text: It helps other people join in
It proves every seat belongs only to us
It gives us a reason to push someone
It means nobody else deserves a place

questions.explanation: Making space helps others participate. We can adjust our belongings without taking over the whole area.

questions.question: Does giving someone a gift make it right to keep shaming them about it?

options.text: Yes, gifts let us control people's feelings
No, giving should not become a way to hurt them
Yes, kindness gives permission to insult
Yes, the receiver loses their right to respect

questions.explanation: A gift should not be used for humiliation. The Quran warns against hurtful reminders attached to charity.

questions.question: Is saying sorry a reason to keep repeating the same hurtful action on purpose?

options.text: Yes, an apology makes every repeated harm acceptable
Yes, words remove the need to change anything
No, we should stop and try to repair the wrong
No, it means we should blame someone else

questions.explanation: Seeking forgiveness goes with taking wrongdoing seriously. Stop the hurtful action and work on putting things right.

questions.question: Does another person's different religion make unfair treatment acceptable?

options.text: Yes, fairness is only for our own group
Yes, difference gives permission to insult
No, but cruelty is a good way to make friends
No, we should still act kindly and fairly

questions.explanation: Different beliefs do not justify unfairness or cruelty. Peaceful people of another faith deserve kind and fair treatment.

questions.question: A classmate says a nickname hurts them. What should you do?

options.text: Stop using it and use a respectful name
Repeat it louder
Teach everyone else to use it
Say their feelings do not matter

questions.explanation: Respect the classmate's feelings and stop the hurtful name. The Quran teaches us to avoid insulting nicknames.

questions.question: Some friends start sharing hurtful gossip about an absent classmate. Which choice is better?

options.text: Add another hurtful story
Avoid joining in and suggest a kinder topic
Invite more children to listen
Turn the gossip into a poster

questions.explanation: Avoid spreading hurtful talk behind someone's back. Changing to a kinder topic can help stop it.

questions.question: A friend lends you crayons for a lesson. What should you do afterward?

options.text: Hide them in your bag to keep
Give them to someone else without asking
Care for them and return them to your friend
Break them so nobody else can use them

questions.explanation: Borrowed crayons are a trust. Treat them carefully and return them to their owner.

questions.question: You count points in a game. A team you dislike earns a point. What is fair?

options.text: Erase it because you dislike them
Give their point to your favorite team
End the game to avoid counting it
Record the point honestly

questions.explanation: Be fair even when feelings are involved. Count the point honestly according to the rules.

questions.question: A friend asks you to help hide another child's schoolbag as a cruel joke. What should you choose?

options.text: Refuse and suggest something kind instead
Help because friends must agree to everything
Hide the bag farther away
Blame the child for having a schoolbag

questions.explanation: We cooperate in good, not in hurting people. If the cruel behavior continues, get a trusted adult's help.

questions.question: You visit a friend's home with your parent. What should you do at the door?

options.text: Run inside before anyone answers
Greet them, ask permission and wait to be invited
Open every room to explore
Insist they must let you enter immediately

questions.explanation: Ask permission and wait. Respecting another family's home follows the Quran's teaching.

questions.question: You finish a learning activity quickly. Which response shows humility?

options.text: Tell everyone else they are worthless
Refuse to speak to anyone still learning
Be pleased without belittling slower classmates
Boast that only you deserve respect

questions.explanation: You can enjoy your progress without looking down on others. Humility leaves room for kindness and respect.

questions.question: During a quiet classroom discussion, how should you speak?

options.text: Shout to drown out every other voice
Scream just to get attention
Make loud noises to annoy classmates
Use a suitable voice and let others speak too

questions.explanation: A voice suited to the setting shows consideration. Give other people a chance to speak and be heard.

questions.question: You are serving yourself a snack. Which choice helps avoid waste?

options.text: Take a suitable amount and ask for more if needed
Take a huge pile just to throw it away
Spill the drink for fun
Throw away untouched food to impress a friend

questions.explanation: Taking a suitable portion helps avoid waste. Ask an adult about saving leftovers safely.

questions.question: A classmate says, "Assalamu alaikum." Which reply fits?

options.text: Go away, your greeting is silly
Wa alaikum assalam
Give me a toy before I answer
Only important people may greet me

questions.explanation: Wa alaikum assalam returns the greeting of peace. We can respond respectfully and warmly.

questions.question: A teacher spends extra time helping you understand a lesson. What can you say?

options.text: Your effort means nothing
You owe me a present too
Thank you for helping me
I will never appreciate your help

questions.explanation: Thanking the teacher recognizes their kindness. Showing gratitude to people follows the Prophet's ﷺ teaching.

questions.question: Two friends argue about whose turn comes next. How can you help?

options.text: Invent an insult for each friend
Tell each one the other hates them
Encourage them to start hitting
Help them check the turn order calmly

questions.explanation: Help find a fair solution rather than adding anger. Ask a teacher if you need help settling the turn order.

questions.question: A friend accidentally knocks over your block tower and apologizes. Which response shows willingness to forgive?

options.text: Accept the apology without seeking revenge
Destroy their belongings in return
Insult their whole family
Plan to embarrass them every day

questions.explanation: An ordinary accident can be met with forgiveness. You may still explain that you felt upset and ask for help rebuilding.

questions.question: You want to win a classroom game. Which choice is honest?

options.text: Move your piece when nobody is looking
Follow the rules without secretly changing the score
Hide the other team's cards
Pretend you answered correctly when you did not

questions.explanation: Honest play avoids cheating. Winning matters less than acting truthfully and fairly.

questions.question: A new classmate has a name from a different language. Which action shows respect?

options.text: Mock the name because it is unfamiliar
Refuse to learn anything about them
Ask politely how to pronounce the name
Say only names like yours matter

questions.explanation: Different backgrounds are a chance to learn about one another. Asking politely about a name shows respect.

questions.question: You are with a parent when someone asks for help. What can you do?

options.text: Shout insults at the person
Laugh at their difficulty
Demand that they entertain you first
Stay with your parent and respond respectfully

questions.explanation: Speak with respect and let your parent guide any help. Needing assistance is not a reason to be humiliated.

questions.question: Your teacher asks everyone to make room for another child in the reading circle. What should you do?

options.text: Move your bag and make suitable space
Spread your belongings across the empty place
Push the child away
Claim the whole circle is yours

questions.explanation: Making room helps another child take part. Follow your teacher's guidance without pushing anyone.

questions.question: With permission, you give a spare notebook to a child who needs one. What should you avoid afterward?

options.text: Letting them use it with dignity
Repeatedly reminding them to make them feel small
Treating them as an equal classmate
Keeping your words respectful

questions.explanation: Give without humiliating the person. A helpful gift should not become a reason for hurtful reminders.

questions.question: You purposely scribbled on a friend's page and now regret it. What is a good next step?

options.text: Hide the page and blame another child
Demand forgiveness while scribbling again
Apologize and ask how to help put it right
Say that their feelings are silly

questions.explanation: Seek forgiveness and work on repairing the wrong. An adult can help you decide how to make things right.

questions.question: A peaceful classmate of another faith joins your group activity. How should you treat them?

options.text: Insult them because their faith differs
Give them unfair rules to make them lose
Refuse basic kindness just because they are different
Include them kindly and apply the same fair rules

questions.explanation: Kindness and fairness apply in dealing with peaceful people of another faith. Treat your classmate respectfully.
